1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""verify-gate-enforcement — closes catalog class G1 (gate-enforcement vacuity)
3	from docs/verification/fv-adversarial-review-playbook.md Part A2.
4	
5	The other anti-vacuity gates (verify-proof-mutation, verify-ledger-consistency,
6	verify-kani-mutation, verify-protocol-models) each ask "is a PROOF hollow?" This
7	one asks the level-up question the 2026-07-01 adversarial round found the tree
8	was blind to: **does the gate that polices hollowness actually RUN on the diff it
9	polices?** A gate that is green-when-run but never fires — wrong `paths:` filter,
10	`continue-on-error`, `workflow_dispatch`-only, or simply not invoked by any job —
11	is exactly as dangerous as a hollow proof (F1: `verify-ledger-consistency` never
12	ran on `AXIOM_STATUS.json`-only edits until an adversarial pass found it by hand).
13	
14	For each gate in scripts/gate_enforcement.json it parses the live CI workflows and
15	asserts the wiring matches the declared enforcement:
16	  * per_pr_blocking — the declared `runs_in` workflow invokes `make <target>`, has a
17	    pull_request trigger covering opening, updates and reopening, the invoking
18	    job/step is NOT `continue-on-error`, and the
19	    trigger covers protected `master` plus every `polices_paths` entry (or has
20	    no branch/path filter). Ordered negative branch/path patterns are rejected.
21	    Every policed path must be covered by the allowlist, when present.
22	    `paths-ignore:` filters are unsupported for per-PR blocking gates.
23	    A gate with `required_context` must additionally match its complete parsed step,
24	    trusted runner, and forbidden-job-key policy; merely retaining the target text
25	    cannot downgrade, relocate, containerize, condition away, or no-op a
26	    load-bearing launcher.
27	  * nightly — the `runs_in` workflow invokes it AND retains its exact reviewed
28	    schedule (the legacy tier includes the documented weekly proxy observation).
29	  * local_documented — deliberately not CI-gated; a NOTE when its registration,
30	    reason and optional workflow metadata are valid. Invalid metadata fails.
31	
32	Robustness (mirrors the sibling gates): a gate whose target no workflow invokes is a
33	HARD FAIL (unwired); the invocation check inspects STEP-level `if:`/`continue-on-error`
34	(not just job-level), so a workflow_dispatch-gated or non-blocking STEP is caught; a
35	final COMPLETENESS pass asserts that every soundness `make verify-*` target invoked by
36	any workflow is enrolled in this manifest (so a CI-wired gate cannot silently escape
37	the manifest — the G1META-1 class). Reverse checks derive the full `make kani`
38	crate surface and every source file in `kani_mutations.json`, so their declared
39	path inventories cannot silently lag the executable gates. Ships `--self-test`
40	negative controls for each reverse check. Read-only — never mutates.
41

43	runner, and absent job controls, rejecting changed shell text/conditions and
44	workflow-level defaults/environment. This includes deliberate expected-failure
45	wrappers already present in production configuration CI. The checker policy pins
46	all registered identities and enforcement levels, including this checker itself;
47	a manifest-only deletion/demotion or completeness waiver fails. A local gate's
48	reason still requires a date or issue reference as documentation hygiene, not as
49	approval. Declared local runs_in metadata must correspond to an invocation.
50	
51	The reviewed checker policy, manifest contracts, and workflow setup remain
52	trusted source. These checks do not interpret arbitrary shell programs, prove
53	hosted branch-protection settings, verify third-party action implementations,
54	or establish that earlier setup steps cannot alter tools or runner state.
55	Context/policy changes require review; they cannot be authorized by this lint.

217	def _covers(filter_globs: list[str], policed: str) -> bool:
218	    """Prove inclusion for equal patterns, catch-all, recursive literal roots,
219	    or a literal suffix under **/. Other glob inclusions fail conservatively.
220	
221	    A literal directory and directory/* do not cover directory/**. GitHub's
222	    path globs match the whole path; * cannot cross a slash.
223	    https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#filter-pattern-cheat-sheet
224	    """
225	    def literal(path: str) -> bool:
226	        return not any(char in path for char in "*?+[]!\\")
227	
228	    for pattern in filter_globs:
229	        if pattern == policed or pattern == "**":
230	            return True
231	        if pattern.endswith("/**"):
232	            prefix = pattern[:-3]
233	            if prefix and literal(prefix) and policed.startswith(prefix + "/"):
234	                return True
235	        if pattern.startswith("**/"):
236	            suffix = pattern[3:]
237	            if literal(suffix) and literal(policed) and (
238	                policed == suffix or policed.endswith("/" + suffix)
239	            ):
240	                return True
241	    return False

276	def _strip_trailing_comment(line: str) -> str:
277	    """Shell comment rules, approximated for a lint: an UNQUOTED `#` at a word
278	    boundary (start of line or after whitespace) starts a comment that eats the
279	    rest of the line — including any surviving `make <gate>` text. Single and
280	    double quotes are tracked so `grep '#x'` / `echo "a #b"` are not corrupted.
281	    A gate neutralized to `true # make gate` is NOT an invocation (#663)."""
282	    out: list[str] = []
283	    in_squote = False
284	    in_dquote = False
285	    for i, ch in enumerate(line):
286	        if in_squote:
287	            if ch == "'":
288	                in_squote = False
289	            out.append(ch)
290	        elif in_dquote:
291	            if ch == '"':
292	                in_dquote = False
293	            out.append(ch)
294	        elif ch == "'":
295	            in_squote = True
296	            out.append(ch)
297	        elif ch == '"':

299	            out.append(ch)
300	        elif ch == "#" and (i == 0 or line[i - 1] in " \t"):
